definitions.meaning: The bare oak shire or BERKSHIRE, so called from a polled oak in Windsor forest, where public meetings were held

source_text: Baroc-scír, e; f. The bare oak shire or BERKSHIRE, so called from a polled oak in Windsor forest, where public meetings were held, Brompt. p. 801. It was most commonly written by the Anglo-Saxons-Barruc, Bearruc, and Bearwucscíre, Chr. 860; Th. 130, 3.
